evals.prompt: I want a heavy-setting LunaTalk card: a city where every district runs on a different calendar. Build the world and relationship engine without turning it into a lore dump.
evals.expected_output: Produces a world-engine packet with player position, core world rule, faction network, locations, compact state model, route seeds, exposition policy, opening implications, token tradeoff, and no MCP calls.
expectations: The output routes to lunatalk-world-engineer or uses world-engine-design.md.
The core world rule creates choices, costs, routes, or consequences rather than only atmosphere.
Each faction or location has a play function, player leverage, pressure, cost, or return hook.
The packet includes a compact state model and 2-4 route seeds with costs and memory.
The output avoids mutating MCP tools and keeps the opening from introducing the full lore list.

evals.prompt: I have a cozy seaside town idea with a lighthouse, market, ghost stories, and neighbors, but it feels bland. Make it playable as a light-setting card without overbuilding.
evals.expected_output: Builds a light-setting world engine with one core rule, one main location, small relationship network, ordinary pressure, state, route hooks, opening implications, and token discipline.
expectations: The output chooses light-setting scope instead of bloating the card into a heavy world.
The world rule and town details create small player actions, trust shifts, routines, or consequences.
The relationship network has wants, pressure moves, and player leverage rather than only neighbor descriptions.
The packet names what lore to keep, delay, or cut.
The output hands off to blueprint or authoring without writing a full card.

evals.prompt: My RPG academy has ten houses, twenty spell types, five currencies, and too many NPCs. Turn the setting into a playable card engine the AI can track.
evals.expected_output: Compresses the RPG/open-world setting into modules, compact state, active locations, faction roles, route seeds, failure pressure, update rules, and token tradeoff.
expectations: The output identifies oversized lore and decorative stats as the failure.
The packet keeps only state that changes access, behavior, risk, route, or cost.
The setting modules are organized by play function rather than encyclopedia category.
The route seeds include trigger, world pressure, player leverage, unlock, cost, memory, and renewed hook.
The repair cuts lore, names, or currencies before cutting agency, consequence, state, or route pressure.
